title: PETRONAS Datapack 2021–2025
description: Consolidated PETRONAS Group financials from public sources: annual reports, media releases, Reuters, Edge Malaysia, The Star, BERNAMA.
note: All figures from PETRONAS Group audited financial statements or official media releases. Gaps marked with null. Replace USER_SUPPLIED entries in fusionreceipt.md with this data.

yearly_data.notes: Revenue and PAT from Q4 2021 cumulative financial statement. Dividend and capex not found in public search.

yearly_data.source: PETRONAS Integrated Report 2022 + Reuters + Edge Malaysia
yearly_data.notes: Record year. RM101.62B PAT (doubled from FY2021). RM50B record dividend. Revenue RM375.3B (+51% YoY). Sources: Business Times Singapore, Edge Malaysia, PETRONAS IR2022.

yearly_data.source: PETRONAS Integrated Report 2023 + Reuters + Malaysian Reserve
yearly_data.notes: PAT RM80.7B (down from FY2022 record). Equity RM451.2B. PETRONAS announced RM300B 5-year capex plan (2023-2027).

yearly_data.source: PETRONAS Media Release 27 Feb 2025 + Reuters + Argus Media + RHB Research
yearly_data.notes: PAT down 17% YoY. Revenue RM305.13B. Capex RM54.22B. Oil fell 4.4% to 813k boepd. Gas rose 3.6%. LNG up 9% to 35.7m tonnes. 21 projects first oil. 14 PSCs signed. RHB: 2H2024 capex RM28.5B (+11% h-o-h, -9% y-o-y). CFO RM102.5B covers capex with ~RM48B surplus.

yearly_data.source: PETRONAS Media Release 27 Feb 2026 + The Star + BERNAMA + LinkedIn analysts
yearly_data.notes: PAT down 18% YoY. Revenue down 17%. Capex RM41.58B (down from RM54.2B — analysts report ~20% cut to RM43B budget). CFO RM85.2B. Equity declining (RM451.2B → RM448.3B). ROACE 8.2% — near/below cost of capital. Edge Malaysia: may not generate sufficient cash for both capex and RM26B dividend.

computed_trends.pat_cagr_2021_2025: computed on load — FY21 48.6B → FY25 45.39B (slight decline over 5 years despite FY22 peak)
computed_trends.revenue_cagr_2021_2025: computed on load — FY21 248B → FY25 266B (modest growth, heavily volatile)
computed_trends.dividend_sustainability: FY22 RM50B dividend exceeded PAT of RM101.6B? No — 49% payout ratio. But FY25 PAT of RM45.4B would be strained by RM26B dividend = 57% payout ratio. FY22 peak was anomalous.
computed_trends.capex_vs_cash_flow: FY24 CFO RM102.5B. FY25 CFO RM85.2B. Capex budget RM70B. Gap narrowing — cash from operations barely exceeds capex in FY25.

key_observations: FY2022 was an anomalous peak (post-pandemic oil price spike). Using it as a baseline is misleading.
PAT has declined for 3 consecutive years: RM101.6B → RM80.7B → RM55.1B → RM45.4B.
Cash from operations (RM85.2B in FY25) barely exceeds capex budget (RM70B), leaving little room for dividends without drawing down reserves.
Equity declined from RM451.2B (FY24) to RM448.3B (FY25) — first decline in recent memory.
Gearing rose from 19.6% to 20.7% — manageable but trending up.
ROACE fell from 9.7% to 8.2% — below cost of capital for many projects.
Oil production declining (813k boepd in FY24, down 4.4%). Gas growing but may not offset.
Edge Malaysia warning (2026): PETRONAS may not generate sufficient cash to cover both RM70B capex and RM26B dividend.
